content.jointProblem: Can site-specific, unsupervised statistical baselines with calibrated thresholds and controlled drift adaptation provide useful, explainable Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP anomaly alerts on ProtoSense without labelled attack training data? The first experiment would test transfer to BACnet and ArmaturaSec hardware using chronological site-traffic holdouts and separate controlled bench scenarios, measuring false alerts per site-day, scenario detection, explanation usefulness, and resource overhead rather than assuming published results will transfer.

rationale.text: Kiss has directly relevant experience developing and operationally validating unsupervised SCADA detectors without labelled attack data.

sources.quote: The project developed threshold calibration procedures for detectors operating without labelled attack data
enabling validation under real traffic conditions.

rationale.text: Her Modbus research provides a concrete starting point for site-specific, field-level baselines whose deviations could be tested as plain-language alert explanations.

sources.quote: This paper describes the construction of per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed.
For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated

rationale.text: Her work addresses both threshold calibration using unlabelled operational data and operator-controlled adaptation to legitimate process changes.

sources.quote: proposes a post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data.
Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed

rationale.text: She has evaluated lightweight detector implementations on constrained ARM hardware, providing relevant deployment experience rather than proof of performance on ProtoSense.

sources.quote: A combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target

rationale.text: Her group offers ICS experimentation infrastructure, and her preference for real deployments aligns with a company-led pilot.

sources.quote: The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
Kiss prefers applied collaborations that result in deployment on real infrastructure rather than purely synthetic experiments.

constraints.text: Training and operational calibration must not require confirmed attack examples; archived traffic must be treated as unlabelled rather than guaranteed clean.

sources.quote: we have nothing labelled as malicious.
if they were compromised they would not know.

constraints.text: The pilot must cover both Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP and learn site-specific behaviour, rather than relying solely on public-dataset performance.

sources.quote: ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic
What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site

constraints.text: Alert acceptance must include an agreed false-alarm burden and explanations understandable to plant managers; detection accuracy alone is insufficient.

sources.quote: it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.
We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Inference must fit the actual on-device resources and embedded Linux integration, without affecting packet forwarding latency; the planned security processor cannot be assumed available.

sources.quote: we have the hardware to run inference on-device
Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build)
a dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency.

constraints.text: Scope must fit one to two part-time company engineers, with archive, bench and firmware access under NDA; use of the university testbed requires a data-sharing agreement.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.
Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.

risks: BACnet detection experience is not demonstrated in the supplied research evidence. Modbus, DNP3 and other protocol results may not transfer; the first experiment must explicitly test BACnet features and controlled scenarios.

Published ARM measurements concern different hardware and workloads. ProtoSense throughput, memory demand and forwarding impact remain unvalidated and require measurement in the first bench experiment.
Undetected compromise in historical captures could become part of the learned baseline. Unlabelled calibration cannot establish that a baseline is attack-free.
Seasonal changes and maintenance may generate nuisance alerts, while overly permissive adaptation could absorb malicious behaviour. Operator acknowledgement and adaptation safeguards need testing.
Controlled injected attacks may not represent real attacks, and anomaly scores do not establish malicious intent. Production detection effectiveness cannot be inferred solely from bench results.
Field-level statistical deviations offer a plausible explanation mechanism, but plant-manager comprehension and usefulness are not established.

Researcher availability and team allocation are unknown. Budget, pilot timetable, current hardware readiness and permissible research use of client captures are also unknown and could prevent execution.
questions: What researcher and student capacity can Kiss commit, and when? Who will own implementation and ongoing model maintenance within ArmaturaSec?
What budget, project duration and pilot decision milestones are available?
What are the actual target appliance CPU, RAM, storage, traffic throughput and latency limits, and is the previously planned security-processor variant now available?
Which sites provide representative Modbus and BACnet archives across operating modes, seasons and maintenance events? Are site identities, device inventories and process-change logs available?
Does client consent permit university access, derived feature extraction and research publication? What NDA, data-sharing, retention and anonymisation terms are required?
Which BACnet services and device behaviours must the first experiment cover, and can representative BACnet devices or simulators be made available for controlled bench scenarios?
What false-alert rate per site-day, detection delay and operator-review effort are acceptable? Which plant managers will evaluate alert explanations?
Which controlled attack and legitimate-change scenarios are authorised for isolated bench testing, and who can adjudicate suspicious historical intervals without assuming they are clean?
Who may approve baseline resets or adaptation after process changes, and how will automatic updates be prevented from learning persistent malicious activity?
